subjects.title: Our Place in Space
subjects.intro: Build a grounded picture of Earth’s neighborhood before moving outward.

chapters.title: Earth
chapters.intro: Earth is a dynamic rocky planet with an atmosphere, oceans, and a magnetic environment.

lessons.title: Earth’s rotation
lessons.summary: Rotation gives us the daily pattern of daylight and darkness.
lessons.question: What creates day and night?

chapters.title: The Moon
chapters.intro: Our Moon preserves a visible record of impacts and is locked in step with Earth.

lessons.title: Reading Moon phases
lessons.summary: Phases are changing views of the Moon’s sunlit half.
lessons.question: What causes Moon phases?

chapters.title: The Solar System
chapters.intro: The Sun, planets, dwarf planets, moons, asteroids, and comets are connected by gravity.

lessons.title: A family held by gravity
lessons.summary: The Sun’s gravity organizes the paths of objects in our planetary system.
lessons.question: What holds the Solar System together?

chapters.title: Planets
chapters.intro: The eight planets range from small rocky worlds to giant planets rich in gas and ice.

lessons.title: Rocky worlds and giant worlds
lessons.summary: Planet composition and distance from the young Sun helped shape the Solar System’s broad families.
lessons.question: Which planets are terrestrial?

chapters.title: Asteroids and Comets
chapters.intro: Small bodies preserve clues about the early Solar System.

lessons.title: Leftovers with a story
lessons.summary: Asteroids and comets are remnants from the Solar System’s formation.
lessons.question: What are asteroids and comets?

subjects.title: Stars & Galaxies
subjects.intro: Follow matter and light from star-forming clouds to the largest structures in the cosmos.

chapters.title: Stars
chapters.intro: Stars are luminous spheres of plasma powered by fusion.

lessons.title: How stars shine
lessons.summary: Fusion in stellar cores releases the energy stars radiate.
lessons.question: What powers a star like the Sun?

chapters.title: Stellar Life Cycles
chapters.intro: Mass guides how a star changes and ends.

lessons.title: A star’s mass matters
lessons.summary: A star’s initial mass is a central factor in its later evolution.
lessons.question: What most affects stellar evolution?

chapters.title: Nebulae
chapters.intro: Nebulae are interstellar clouds connected to star birth and stellar endings.

lessons.title: Clouds between stars
lessons.summary: Gas and dust clouds can be nurseries for new stars or material from old ones.
lessons.question: What is a nebula?

chapters.title: Galaxies
chapters.intro: Galaxies gather stars, gas, dust, and more through gravity.

lessons.title: The Milky Way in context
lessons.summary: Our Solar System sits in the Milky Way, one galaxy among many.
lessons.question: What holds galaxies together?

chapters.title: Black Holes
chapters.intro: Black holes are compact objects whose gravity profoundly affects nearby matter and light.

lessons.title: Gravity beyond the horizon
lessons.summary: Beyond an event horizon, light cannot escape a black hole.
lessons.question: Can light escape beyond an event horizon?

subjects.title: How We Explore
subjects.intro: Explore the tools, people, and measurement systems that turn distant places into evidence.

chapters.title: Rockets
chapters.intro: Rockets move by expelling mass and conserving momentum.

lessons.title: Motion without air
lessons.summary: Rockets work in space because exhaust carries momentum away.
lessons.question: Do rockets need air outside them?

chapters.title: Spacecraft
chapters.intro: Spacecraft carry instruments, computers, power systems, and communications into challenging environments.

lessons.title: Signals across space
lessons.summary: Radio communication links spacecraft with teams on Earth.
lessons.question: What do many spacecraft use to communicate?

chapters.title: Telescopes
chapters.intro: Telescopes turn faint light into measurements across the electromagnetic spectrum.

lessons.title: Observing from above the atmosphere
lessons.summary: Space telescopes can access or sharpen observations that the atmosphere limits.
lessons.question: Why place some telescopes in space?

chapters.title: Human Spaceflight
chapters.intro: Astronauts rely on life-support systems and carefully designed vehicles.

lessons.title: Living in microgravity
lessons.summary: Orbiting crews feel weightless because they are in continuous free-fall around Earth.
lessons.question: Is gravity absent in orbit?

chapters.title: Exploration Missions
chapters.intro: Missions use complementary approaches to investigate worlds and the wider universe.

lessons.title: Choosing the right mission
lessons.summary: Orbiters, landers, rovers, and telescopes answer different scientific questions.
lessons.question: Why use different mission types?
answers: They all do the same task
